title: handoff-day-kvcache-batching-kernel-observations
content:
Handoff notes from night shift (2026-03-11) — quick observations and action items

Summary: overnight run flagged two small regressions after kernel patch r9712 landed in canary: a sporadic KV-cache memory growth on long-lived chat sessions and an increase in 95th/99th token latency for small (<=128 token) requests when batching window set to 15ms. No customer-facing errors were reported, but we rolled the patch back on canary and opened a limited rollback on a subset of dedicated pools.

What I (on-call) observed:
- At ~01:40 UTC saw gradual increase in GPU memory on canary-hosts-2/3; top process is serve-runtime:worker. Memory climbed ~120MB over 3h on sessions that used sticky KV (chat continuity).
- Batching traces show that for short requests we sometimes waited full batching-window (15ms) even with only 1 incoming request — surfaced as tail latency spike in per-route dashboard.
- Kernel r9712 introduced fused_attention_v2 (expected +6% throughput), but it also increased per-layer temporary buffer by ~8MB per layer. With 24-layer models this adds up (~192MB), which aligns with observed memory bump when runtime toggled to fused_attention_v2.
- KV-cache leak appears different: heap snapshots indicate a small number of KV shards not being freed when sessions are evicted via TTL; suspect race between TTL eviction and async checkpoint write.

Repro steps I ran (quick):
- Replayed long chat session trace: tools/run_replay.sh --trace=long_chat_20260310.json --host=canary-hosts-2 --keep-connections
- Microbench for batching latency: tools/microbench_batching.py --model=redwood-7b-v1 --seq=64 --concurrency=1 --window_ms=15,10,5
- Memory profiling: python3 -m tracemalloc serve_runtime_worker.py --tracefile=memdump_canary_03011

Findings from repros:
- When window_ms=15, P95 token latency increased by ~18% vs 5ms for short requests in our microbench. (5ms window reduces batching inefficiency but increases CPU interrupts).
- Replaying long chat produced orphaned KV shards in memdump: keys show TTL=0 but refcount != 0. Stack traces point to async_checkpoint::on_write_complete callback.
- Switching fused_attention_v2 off in runtime flags restored memory baseline but CPU throughput dropped to pre-patch levels.

Immediate actions taken overnight:
- Rolled back r9712 on canary pool at 03:15 UTC (flag flipped to fused_attention_v1). Memory stabilized within 20 minutes.
- Lowered default batching window for canary route '/chat/stream' from 15ms -> 8ms as a temporary mitigation to reduce tail latency; opened ticket to evaluate adaptive windowing.
- Added extra telemetry to trace KV eviction path: emitted event kv.eviction.attempt and kv.eviction.complete with session_id and shard_count in debug telemetry.
- Created SRV-4123 (Jira) to investigate KV shard refcount race; assigned to Chen Wei.

Notes for next shift / handoff:
- Chen: start with SRV-4123 reproduce steps. Prioritize capturing concurrent eviction + checkpoint scenario. If repro is flaky, instrument checkpoint write to hold completion for 50ms to amplify race.
- Luca: run extended microbench with adaptive-window flag on canary (flag: --adaptive-batching=true) and measure P50/P95/P99 across intervals (1h run). Compare cost/latency tradeoff.
- Maya: coordinate with infra to snapshot canary-hosts-2 mem state before any more reboots. We may want to run leak-finder script that allocates dummy sessions and force-evict them.

Longer term / follow-ups:
- Evaluate making fused_attention_v2 allocate temporaries in a different memory pool and release earlier to avoid long-lived spikes. Potential kernel-level change or runtime hook (PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/978).
- Prototype adaptive-batching that short-circuits window when queue depth is low (threshold=1 after 3 consecutive windows). This may retain throughput gains while avoiding tail latency for short requests.
- Add automated regression test in perf-bench CI: run microbench with window_ms sweep and assert P95 <= baseline*1.1 for short-request profiles.

Open questions / things to check:
- Could the checkpoint write path be holding onto shared_ptrs to KV shards? Need code review of async_checkpoint in storage/kvcache.cpp.
- Should the default batching window be lowered globally or only for chat/stream endpoints? Tradeoffs for CPU vs latency.
- Any correlation with specific GPU types (A100 vs A10)? Overnight canary hosts are mixed; verify whether memory bump correlates to A100 memory allocator behavior.

Incident timeline (short):
- 01:40 UTC — memory drift alerted (canary-hosts-2)
- 02:05 UTC — on-call begins triage, starts replay
- 02:55 UTC — traces point to fused_attention_v2 patch; confirm patch active on canary
- 03:15 UTC — rollback of r9712 on canary
- 03:45 UTC — memory stabilizes; dashboards show tail latency still slightly elevated for '/chat/stream'
- 04:10 UTC — temporary batching_window lowered to 8ms on canary

Small debugging snippets (commands to re-run):
- kubectl -n serve-runtime exec -it canary-hosts-2 -- bash -c "ps aux | grep serve-runtime"
- tools/run_replay.sh --trace=long_chat_20260310.json --host=canary-hosts-2
- ./perf/microbench --model=redwood-7b-v1 --batch-window-ms=8 --seq-length=64 --duration=3600
- gdb --pid <pid> -ex "thread apply all bt full" -ex detach -ex quit (if we need deep native stack)

Action items (owners):
- Chen Wei: full KV eviction repro and fix plan (SRV-4123) — due 2026-03-15
- Luca Romano: adaptive-batching experiment report and metrics (bench results, cost delta) — due 2026-03-14
- Maya Thompson: preserve canary mem snapshot and run leak-finder script — due 2026-03-12 (ASAP)
- Asha (me): follow up on PR 978, help coordinate kernel/rt patches review and perf run — ongoing

Misc notes / context:
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime called out around 01:50 UTC, thread id: Mar11-kv-leak.
- There's an internal note in PR 978 about fused_attention_v2 using a temporary buffer pool; authors (Ravi) suggested it was safe but may have missed TTL interplay.

If you pick this up: start with the repro steps, then binary search between kernel flag and runtime eviction path. If you need more capacity to reproduce, spin up a canary-scale test cluster using infra/scaleup_playbook.md (reach out to SRE on-call).

End of handoff. Ping me in slack if anything blocks.

-- Asha
